text: Expectations is the debut studio album by American singer-songwriter Bebe Rexha, released on June 22, 2018, by Warner Bros. Records. The album was announced after the success of her collaboration with country duo Florida Georgia Line on "Meant to Be." It went on pre-order on April 13, 2018, accompanied by two promotional singles: "Ferrari" and "2 Souls on Fire," the latter featuring Quavo of Migos. The album includes the singles "I Got You" and "Meant to Be," the latter from All Your Fault: Pt. 2. It also features appearances by rappers Quavo and Tory Lanez, along with Florida Georgia Line. Expectations received generally positive reviews from music critics, who praised its production and Rexha's vocal performance, though some criticized its lyricism. According to Metacritic, the album received an average score of 65 based on six reviews, indicating "generally favorable reviews." AllMusic's Neil Z. Yeung viewed it as an improvement over her previous EPs, calling it mature and forward-thinking pop with introspective themes, though noting the middle section stalls momentum. Craig Jenkins from Vulture praised the album's versatility and memorable hooks, describing it as "one of the week's easiest pleasures." Ilana Kaplan and Nick Hasted from The Independent highlighted the ballads "Grace" and "Knees," calling the album "full of flawed, self-deprecating and boundary-pushing pop offerings." Mike Nied from Idolator said the album "perfectly captures the superstar's ethos" and praised Rexha's voice, though he noted "Meant to Be" feels out of place. Nick Levine from NME perceived Rexha as an "emo singer," while Refinery29's Courtney E. Smith described her as an "anti-hero" and a "dangerous woman" exploring themes of depression and unpredictability, noting a lack of autobiographical elements. Rolling Stone's Sarah Grant described the album as Rexha painting herself as a heroine trapped in her own ivory tower, with a sensitive tone rather than vengeance, calling it an "impressive debut album full of nostalgic heartache." Tommy Monroe from The Quietus acknowledged a few tracks lacking energy but called Rexha "no ordinary singer" and a "chameleon" capable of adapting to various sounds and tempos. Laura Snapes of The Guardian criticized the overuse of Auto-Tune and Rexha's "desperate search of an identity," citing "Ferrari" as the "only remotely distinctive song." The album debuted at number 13 on the US Billboard 200, earning 24,000 album-equivalent units (including 10,000 pure album sales) in its first week. It also debuted at number 14 on the Billboard Canadian Albums chart. As of January 2019, the album had sold 604,000 units in the US (with 37,000 in pure album sales). On October 23, 2020, it was certified platinum by the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA) for combined sales and album-equivalent units exceeding one million in the United States. "I'm a Mess" was released as the lead single on June 15, following an early radio release in the United States, and peaked at number 35 on the Billboard Hot 100, becoming Rexha's first top 40 hit as a solo lead artist. "Ferrari" has since received a vertical video.
